person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: inorganic crystal structures and whether a graph neural network can predict which are thermodynamically stable
span.quote: In particular, GNoME models found 2.2 million crystal structures stable with respect to the Materials Project. Of these, 381,000 entries live on the updated convex hull as newly discovered materials.

span.label: whether machine learning can estimate stability against the convex hull accurately enough to guide discovery, which prior methods could not
span.quote: Although data-driven methods that aid in further materials discovery have been pursued, thus far, machine-learning techniques have been ineffective in estimating stability (decomposition energy) with respect to the convex hull of energies from competing phases.

span.label: 2.2 million structures stable with respect to the Materials Project, of which 381,000 sit on the updated convex hull, plus learned interatomic potentials from the resulting dataset
span.quote: In particular, GNoME models found 2.2 million crystal structures stable with respect to the Materials Project. Of these, 381,000 entries live on the updated convex hull as newly discovered materials.

span.label: existence
span.quote: In particular, GNoME models found 2.2 million crystal structures stable with respect to the Materials Project. Of these, 381,000 entries live on the updated convex hull as newly discovered materials.

span.label: emergent out-of-distribution generalisation in a graph network trained at scale
span.quote: Moreover, these networks develop emergent out-of-distribution generalization. For example, GNoME enables accurate predictions of structures with 5+ unique elements (despite omission from training), providing one of the first strategies to efficiently explore this chemical space.

span.label: rounds of active learning: generate candidates, filter with graph networks, verify the survivors with DFT, retrain on the result
span.term: rounds of active learning: generate candidates, filter with graph networks, verify the survivors with DFT, retrain on the result
span.quote: The energy of the filtered candidates is computed using DFT, both verifying model predictions and serving as a data flywheel to train more robust models on larger datasets in the next round of active learning.

span.label: DFT verifies the model's filtered candidates and the verified results become the next round's training data, so the same computation both audits the model and improves it
span.quote: The energy of the filtered candidates is computed using DFT, both verifying model predictions and serving as a data flywheel to train more robust models on larger datasets in the next round of active learning.

span.label: prediction quality improves as a power law in the amount of data, matching what has been observed in language and vision rather than being specific to materials
span.quote: Consistent with observations in other domains of machine learning, we observe that our neural networks predictions improve as a power law with the amount of data.

span.label: the discovered materials can themselves be bumped off the convex hull by future work - stability is a claim about a catalogue at a moment
span.quote: Consistent with other literature on structure prediction, the GNoME materials could be bumped off the convex hull by future discoveries, similar to how GNoME displaces at least 5,000 ‘stable’ materials from the Materials Project and the OQMD.

span.label: the experimental-match count is a lower bound, because the compositional match is enforced strictly
span.quote: Given that we are enforcing a strict compositional match, our matching process is still relatively conservative and is likely to yield a lower bound.

span.label: the matching answer moves by about 100 structures depending on parser and matcher tolerance settings
span.quote: For both modules, we tried using the default settings as well as more tolerant settings that improve structure parsing and matching (higher occupancy tolerance in CIF parsing to fix cases with >1.0 total occupancy and allowing supercell and subset comparison in matching). The latter resulted in a slight increase (about 100) in the number of matched structures with respect to the default settings.

span.label: the discovery functional was chosen for a speed-accuracy trade-off rather than accuracy, and 84% rather than 100% survive the more accurate one
span.quote: Standard projector augmented wave (PAW)-Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof (PBE) potentials provided a speed–accuracy trade-off suited for large-scale discovery, but the r2SCAN functional provides a more accurate meta-generalized gradient approximation.

span.label: neural scaling laws, carried from language and vision into materials-stability prediction
span.quote: Consistent with observations in other domains of machine learning, we observe that our neural networks predictions improve as a power law with the amount of data.

span.label: recomputation under the more accurate r2SCAN functional, to test whether discovery overfitted the cheaper PBE one
span.note: eliminates: a discovery set that exists only under the cheap functional it was searched with · outcome: partial
span.quote: 84% of the discovered binaries and ternary materials also present negative phase-separation energies (as visualized in Fig. 2d, comparable with a 90% ratio in the Materials Project but operating at a larger scale). 86.8% of tested quaternaries also remain stable on the r2SCAN convex hull.

span.label: an explicit check that model-based exploration did not overfit the simulation parameters
span.note: eliminates: model-based exploration finding materials that are artefacts of the simulation parameters it was trained against · outcome: held
span.quote: We also validate predictions to ensure that model-based exploration did not overfit simulation parameters. We focus on the choice of functional.

span.label: matching against crystals experimentally realised by other groups after the training snapshot
span.note: eliminates: a match rate inflated by structures the model could have seen, since these were realised experimentally after the training snapshot · outcome: held
span.quote: Of the experimental structures aggregated in the ICSD, 736 match structures that were independently obtained through GNoME.

span.label: comparison against compositions added to the Materials Project after the March 2021 snapshot
span.note: eliminates: a match rate computed only against the database the model was trained on · outcome: held
span.quote: Similarly, of the 3,182 compositions added to the Materials Project since the snapshot, 2,202 are available in the GNoME database and 91% match on structure.

span.label: a sensitivity check on the parser and matcher tolerances used to count experimental matches
span.note: eliminates: an experimental match count that exists only at one parser and matcher tolerance setting · outcome: partial
span.quote: For both modules, we tried using the default settings as well as more tolerant settings that improve structure parsing and matching (higher occupancy tolerance in CIF parsing to fix cases with >1.0 total occupancy and allowing supercell and subset comparison in matching). The latter resulted in a slight increase (about 100) in the number of matched structures with respect to the default settings.

span.label: convex hull
span.quote: Although data-driven methods that aid in further materials discovery have been pursued, thus far, machine-learning techniques have been ineffective in estimating stability (decomposition energy) with respect to the convex hull of energies from competing phases.

span.label: hit rate
span.quote: Final GNoME models accurately predict energies to 11 meV atom−1 and improve the precision of stable predictions (hit rate) to above 80% with structure and 33% per 100 trials with composition only, compared with 1% in previous work.

span.label: active learning
span.quote: The energy of the filtered candidates is computed using DFT, both verifying model predictions and serving as a data flywheel to train more robust models on larger datasets in the next round of active learning.

span.label: GNoME

span.label: Materials Project
span.quote: In particular, GNoME models found 2.2 million crystal structures stable with respect to the Materials Project. Of these, 381,000 entries live on the updated convex hull as newly discovered materials.

span.label: r2SCAN
span.quote: 84% of the discovered binaries and ternary materials also present negative phase-separation energies (as visualized in Fig. 2d, comparable with a 90% ratio in the Materials Project but operating at a larger scale). 86.8% of tested quaternaries also remain stable on the r2SCAN convex hull.

span.label: experimental match
span.quote: By rounding to nearest integer formulas, we found 4,235 composition matches with materials discovered by GNoME. Of these, 4,180 are successfully parsed for structure.

span.label: prototypes
span.quote: Clustering by means of prototype analysis supports the diversity of discovered crystals with GNoME, leading to more than 45,500 novel prototypes in Fig. 2c (a 5.6 times increase from 8,000 of the Materials Project), which could not have arisen from full substitutions or prototype enumeration.

span.label: 'stable' sense 1 = below the convex hull OF A PRIOR CATALOGUE - 2.2 million structures
span.quote: In particular, GNoME models found 2.2 million crystal structures stable with respect to the Materials Project. Of these, 381,000 entries live on the updated convex hull as newly discovered materials.

span.label: 'stable' sense 2 = ON the UPDATED convex hull after this work - 381,000 entries, six times fewer
span.quote: In particular, GNoME models found 2.2 million crystal structures stable with respect to the Materials Project. Of these, 381,000 entries live on the updated convex hull as newly discovered materials.

span.label: stability is REVOCABLE: these materials can be bumped off the hull by future discoveries, exactly as this work bumps off 5,000 others
span.quote: Consistent with other literature on structure prediction, the GNoME materials could be bumped off the convex hull by future discoveries, similar to how GNoME displaces at least 5,000 ‘stable’ materials from the Materials Project and the OQMD.

span.label: 'meaningfully stable' = distributed like known stable phases, not merely filling gaps in the hull
span.quote: The similarities in distribution suggest that the found materials are meaningfully stable with respect to competing phases and not just ‘filling in the convex hull.’

span.label: 'experimental match' = integer-rounded composition match AND a pymatgen structure match, declared a lower bound
span.quote: Given that we are enforcing a strict compositional match, our matching process is still relatively conservative and is likely to yield a lower bound.
